newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Corp raises Israel Chemical stake.
newsitem.headline: Israel Corp raises Israel Chemical stake.

text.p: Israel Corp completed a deal on Sunday that boosts its holding in Israel Chemicals to 41.9 percent and seals its status as the biggest player in the Israeli privatisation process.
Government officials hailed the sale as an important step forward in their effort to revive the flagging privatisation process.

In a ceremony at the Treasury, the holding company handed over a cheque for 667 million shekels ($198 million) for 17 percent of Israel Chemicals, a producer of fertilisers and chemicals mined from the Dead Sea.
Israel Corp already controlled 24.9 percent of the company, which it bought in 1995.

"The transaction that we completed today to sell 17 percent of Israel Chemicals to Israel Corp, together with the sale we did in 1995, makes the privatisation of Israel Chemicals one of the biggest privatisations in the State of Israel, no doubt the biggest," said Treasury Director-General Shai Talmon.

The ceremony was a subdued affair, just three days after the death of Israel Corp's billionaire chairman Shoul Eisenberg. Eisenberg, who suffered a heart attack last Thursday in Beijing, was to be buried in Israel later on Sunday.
The Treasury said the two sides were forced to complete the sale so soon after Eisenberg's death because Sunday was the last day Israel Corp could exercise its option on the shares.

Israel Chemicals was valued at its average Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) price over the previous 90 days, or 3.9 billion shekels. To finance the acquisition, Israel Corp said it had taken a $128 million long-term bank loan and financed the rest through short-term bank borrowings.
The government retains 31.5 percent of Israel Chemicals. Another 25 percent is traded on the TASE and the rest held in trust for employees.
Israel Corp took the option when it acquired its 24.9 percent controlling stake in Israel Chemicals from the government in February 1995 for $230.3 million.
Israel Corp also holds 25.1 percent of Properties and Development Co, which it acquired from the government as part of a group, paying $63 million.

In addition, Israel Corp controls about 50 percent of Zim Israel Navigation, one of the world's largest shipping companies, and 26 percent of Oil Refineries Ltd, which has a monopoly in petroleum refining. The government holds the remaining shares.
Both partnerships pre-date Israel's privatisation programme, launched in the late 1980s. Earlier this year the Government Corporations Authority said it hoped to sell its shares in Zim.

"Along with the privatisation completed by the Government Corporations Authority selling Yozma last week, (the Israel Chemicals) sales marks a good start for 1997 and offers hope that the target the government has taken upon itself to raise four billion shekels for the budget can be realised by the end of the year," said Talmon.
The government sold Yozma, a venture capital fund, to Ofer Brothers Investments for 50 million shekels.
Besides Zim, the government is hoping to sell shares in Bezeq Israel Telecom and as many as three state-owned banks.
